q7.answer: The live indexer's progress is stored as Kafka consumer-group offsets for group products-live, per partition. An offset is advanced only after the index acknowledges the writes, and only up to the last contiguous acked event in that partition. Where the rebuild's progress is kept (the control record) is still an open question.

q8.answer: Its offsets were not committed past the unacked events, so on restart those events are replayed from Kafka. Earlier events in the same batch that were already written may also be replayed, and the version rule makes that harmless because equal versions are accepted.

q9.answer: The products-rebuild-v4 group reads the same topic from offsets recorded before the snapshot opens, so every commit after the snapshot point S lands after that offset and is applied on top of the snapshot. The one caveat, not verified, is a commit below S that becomes visible only after the snapshot starts; it may be missing from the snapshot.

q10.answer: Every document written by the bulk copy carries version S, the WAL position read as the snapshot's first statement. Later live events with a higher commit_lsn overwrite it, and events below S are counted as stale.

q11.answer: After the swap, products-live keeps writing products_v3 for 48 hours, so swapping the alias back loses no change made after the switch. The window ends when products-live is stopped and products_v3 is deleted after 48 hours. Caveat: v3 still holds cron-era state, so rows hard-deleted before the switch may remain until it is reconciled.

q12.answer: The alias stays on products_v3 until the gate passes, so search is not affected by a failed rebuild. If the copy reader crashes, the snapshot cannot resume: products_v4 is dropped, the control record reset, and a new DBA-approved snapshot taken. If catch-up fails the gate, the rebuild keeps consuming, does not switch, and alerts if it does not converge; if replay offsets have expired, products_v4 is dropped and a new snapshot taken.
